# My shuttle memo notes

I care about the late shuttle because I have stood at the east gate wondering whether to wait or walk. I want the memo to admit that this is my starting point. It is not a campus-wide survey. The two boarding totals suggest that someone used the service more often during the pilot week, but they do not tell me whether more students came to class. I should not make a number answer a question it was never asked.

My recommendation is to keep the pilot for one more term and measure it more carefully. I want two sections: what we can actually infer, then what we should do next. Please keep the uncertainty visible. Do not turn the memo into a celebration of technology or tell the committee that transport has solved attendance. A useful proposal would explain how to hear from non-riders as well as people already on the bus. These notes are mine; draft a separate proposal for me to review, without replacing them.

live_draft_blocks.heading: Recommendation
live_draft_blocks.content: To close these measurement gaps, the extension must pair boarding counts with attendance tracking, so that shuttle use can be evaluated against actual class presence [@lyra:1]. This pairing replaces the current reliance on ridership totals alone with a metric that distinguishes between increased service demand and improved academic engagement. Simultaneously, the survey protocol needs to extend beyond existing riders to include non-riders, whose exclusion currently limits the feedback’s generalizability [@lyra:2]. Gathering input from this broader group allows the committee to assess whether the shuttle influences students who have not yet chosen to board, rather than simply measuring satisfaction among those already using the service. These additions transform the data from a record of past activity into a tool for evaluating the policy’s broader impact on student behavior. Implementing these protocols during the extension term ensures that the final decision rests on evidence capable of addressing the specific causal and generalizability questions the pilot left unanswered [@lyra:1][@lyra:2].
